requirement: The tilt-actuation subsystem shall sweep the wing-tilt servo through the full 0° to 90° tilt range at the specified wing tilt actuation rate, and it shall sweep the tail-tilt actuator through the full 0° to 90° tilt range at the specified tail tilt position response rate, and it shall report tilt-range compliance to the flight control system.

instances.explanation: the noun stack 'wing tilt actuation rate' can bind as the rate of (wing-tilt actuation) — how fast the wing tilts — or as an (actuation-rate) parameter belonging to a separate 'wing tilt' category, so which quantity is bounded is unclear.

the four-noun compound can stack as (tail-tilt) (position-response-rate) — how fast the position reading responds — or as (tail-tilt-position) (response-rate) — how fast the mechanism responds to a commanded position — so the specified quantity is not uniquely recoverable.

requirement: If a tilt actuator fault is detected, the tilt-actuation subsystem shall promptly command the affected actuator to hold its last commanded tilt position until the flight control system issues a recovery command.

instances.explanation: 'promptly' gives no numeric response-time bound for reacting to the fault, so the required reaction latency could be read as 10 ms or as 1 s depending on the reader.

requirement: Building on the tilt-actuation command interface established above, the tilt-actuation subsystem shall sense actuator position to within the accuracy required for closed-loop tilt control. The ground station shall also receive tilt-position telemetry so that the airframe's true tilt state can be verified independently of the onboard controller.

instances.explanation: 'also' presupposes some prior telemetry or reporting obligation this is adding to, but it is unclear whether it presupposes the sensing obligation in the previous sentence or a separate, already-established ground telemetry feed.

'position' is polysemous between the angular tilt reading (the commanded/actual tilt angle) and the physical mounting location of the sensing hardware, so 'sense actuator position' could mean angle-sensing or location verification.

'the ground station' metonymically stands in for either the physical GCS hardware receiving the data link or the human operator/mission-control crew reading it, leaving who or what must 'receive' the telemetry unclear.

'the airframe' is used as a stand-in for the aircraft's tilt-actuation and structural systems collectively, so it is unclear whether 'the airframe's true tilt state' means the wing-tilt angle, the tail-tilt angle, or a combined structural attitude state.

nuclear_sentences: The tilt-actuation subsystem shall sense actuator position to within the accuracy required for closed-loop tilt control.
The ground station shall receive tilt-position telemetry so that the airframe's true tilt state can be verified independently of the onboard controller.

requirement: The tilt-actuation subsystem shall accept a tilt command from the controller and shall drive the wing-tilt servo to the commanded tilt angle, and it shall drive the tail-tilt actuator to the commanded tilt angle. The wing-tilt servo shall reach the commanded angle faster than the tail-tilt actuator, and the subsystem shall not exceed the commanded tilt angle without confirmation from the controller once tilt mode is engaged.

instances.explanation: 'the controller' is a bare common noun with no which-one binding — it could be the flight control system's autopilot or a dedicated local tilt-actuation controller board — so the source of the command is unclear.

instances.trigger: shall not exceed the commanded tilt angle without confirmation
instances.explanation: the scope of the negation is unclear: it could mean the subsystem may exceed the commanded angle only with confirmation (a conditional permission), or that it must never exceed the angle and must separately always act without waiting for confirmation.

'mode' is polysemous between the actuator's local operating mode (e.g., position-control vs. rate-control) and the aircraft's overall flight mode (VTOL, transition, cruise), so which kind of 'mode' must be 'engaged' is unclear.

'a tilt command' can be read as a specific command token issued in the moment, or as any instance of the general class/type of tilt commands the interface accepts, so what is being accepted is ambiguous between a token and a type.

the elided comparison is recoverable two ways: the wing-tilt servo reaches its own commanded angle faster than the tail-tilt actuator reaches its own commanded angle, or faster than the tail-tilt actuator reaches the wing's commanded angle.

nuclear_sentences: The tilt-actuation subsystem shall accept a tilt command from the controller.

requirement: When commanded to a trim point, the tilt-actuation subsystem shall complete the wing/tail tilt transition within an acceptable settling time, and once transition is complete it shall hold tilt position there. This may be relaxed as required near the edges of the transition speed band, and similarly for the reverse transition back to hover.

instances.explanation: 'This' has more than one candidate antecedent — the acceptable settling-time bound, the hold-position obligation, or the whole preceding compound requirement — so what may be relaxed is unclear.
'acceptable settling time' expresses a personal/engineering-judgment threshold with no numeric bound, so what counts as acceptable is reader-dependent.
'as required' leaves relaxation of the settling-time bound optional and unquantified, with no stated criterion for when it is invoked.
'a trim point' can be read as a specific one of the eight defined trim points (a token) or as the general category/type of trim condition, leaving which trim point(s) the obligation covers unclear.
'similarly' asserts a resemblance to the preceding relaxation without stating what specifically is similar or by how much, making the reverse-transition allowance a matter of subjective judgment.

nuclear_sentences: When commanded to a trim point, the tilt-actuation subsystem shall complete the wing/tail tilt transition within an acceptable settling time.
Once transition is complete, the tilt-actuation subsystem shall hold tilt position at that trim point.

requirement: While the aircraft is operating in transition mode, tilt-position feedback shall be provided to the power and energy subsystem so that motor commands can be adjusted if needed.

'if needed' makes the downstream adjustment of motor commands optional and gives no criterion for when it is needed, so it is unverifiable whether the obligation was met.

instances.explanation: 'trim' is a homonym with unrelated meanings here — the aircraft's equilibrium/trim flight condition versus a small mechanical trim adjustment of a control surface — so 'trim position' and 'trim schedule' could refer to either sense.

nuclear_sentences: While the aircraft is in forward flight, the tilt-actuation subsystem shall hold both actuators at the trim position established for cruise.
